ai.title: DeepSeek Open-Sources dsh-superagent, a Router-Worker Coding Agent
ai.brief: The DeepSeek Harness team just released dsh-superagent , an MIT-licensed research prototype. DeepSeek dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository. It is packaged as a bundle for DeepSeek Harness . It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. It turns allowed requests into parallel work items, each in its own agent session. The release shipped alongside a design post, Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System . 0, released as 1 commit under MIT. It uses whatever model the Harness profile is set to. Runs on: Your own machine, as a dedicated DeepSeek Harness profile. 48+. Performance: In DeepSeek’s simulation, it finished tasks far faster under a noisy message stream than a single-session agent. 9x faster). Worst: Tested only on synthetic messages and simulated tools. Real coding quality was not measured. What is DeepSeek dsh-superagent? It is a GitHub agent that waits to be asked.

sec.title: SMS of Death: Android under attack, an invisible SMS can block calls and emergency services
sec.brief: S. S. S. gov Domains Ads or Surveillance? S. CISA adds Google Brotli and Adobe Commerce and Magento flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog A specially manipulated SMS message is enough to crash Android’s phone service, interrupt ongoing calls, and temporarily render the smartphone unusable. The attack requires no interaction from the victim and can even compromise the ability to contact emergency services. The vulnerability, dubbed the SMS of Death, is bringing renewed attention to the security of the messaging system in Android smartphones. The issue, documented by independent researcher Mark Blaszczyk, allows a remote attacker to cause a disruption in phone service by sending a single, specially crafted WAP Push message.
